title: Grateful Dead Live at Oakland Auditorium Arena on 1982-12-27

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear matrix mix captures a tight 1982 set with smoking Scarlet Fire, Birdsong, Bertha and a powerful Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its clean, well‑balanced mix that lets every instrument shine, while the performance is described as tight, energetic and full of purpose – especially Garcia’s committed solos on Scarlet Fire and Birdsong. Standout moments include Bertha, Let It Grow, Sugar Magnolia and a rousing Other One; only the fast version of Playin’ in the Band feels a bit rushed.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (average >4.5) and uniformly enthusiastic comments about both the music and the mix indicate a strong show with excellent recording quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers highlight crystal‑clear vocals, a great sounding mix, crisp balance between audience ambience and soundboard clarity; no significant dropouts or muddiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First two‑thirds of the show are focused and tight, building into a powerful second set where the tribal Fire, engaging drums and strong finish keep momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solos are described as fully committed, each note evolving with purpose; his tone is called perfect and every note played to perfection.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir “wails Donna back into the stone age” and proves he can deliver powerful vocals; his playing is praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s keyboards are called “intricate, splashy” and tightly connected with Bob, adding depth to the sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are noted as engaging and strong, driving the tribal Fire and overall energy of the show.
